title: fix(cli): os migrate meta prints the manual change that judges an applied edit beside that edit, marked review
body:
Fixes #20620
Clause-②: no

Direction 2 of triage's first grade on #20620 (comment `5888087153`): 「Where an applied conversion has a semantic sibling that judges it, print the sibling beside the applied edit, marked **review**.」 It pairs through the declared `SemanticMigration.conversionIds` only, never through text mentions (release `5916560364`). Direction 1 (order) landed in PR #20691. Direction 3 (write-back) is not taken by triage, so this PR closes the card.

## What changes

`printMigrationReport` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts`), the human face of `os migrate meta --from N`, now prints group 2 through `printAppliedEdits`. Under each run of applied edits by one conversion, it prints one review line for every semantic entry that names that conversion in `conversionIds`:

```text
  Applied 3 mechanical change(s):
    • dashboards[0].refreshIntervalSeconds: refreshInterval → refreshIntervalSeconds (dashboard-refresh-interval-to-refresh-interval-seconds)
    • flows[0].nodes[1].config.mode: mode unset (2 conditioned out-edges; every one whose condition held was taken) → inclusive (flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit)
    • flows[1].nodes[1].config.mode: mode unset (2 conditioned out-edges; every one whose condition held was taken) → inclusive (flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit)
      ↳ review the 2 edits above against the manual change [protocol 18] flow.nodes[].config.mode (decision) — an OMITTED mode on a decision that branches on its out-edges and carries two or more conditioned ones → nothing, where the out-edge conditions partition (exactly one can hold for any record): […]
```

(The review line is cut at `[…]` here. It is printed in full.)

- **It is a copy, not a move.** The review line repeats the entry's `[protocol N] surface → replacement` headline, which is the line group 3 prints for that entry. Group 3 still prints every entry, byte for byte, under the same `N manual change(s) require your judgment:` count, so ADR-0087 D3's "never silence" holds. The `why` and `verify` lines are found in group 3 under the same headline.
- **Declared links only.** `judgesByConversion` reads `todo.conversionIds`, which the chain copies from the entry. Nothing matches prose.
- **Nothing else moves.** Every edit line is byte-identical and in chain order, and the group 2 header count is unchanged. An edit that no entry judges prints with nothing under it. `--json`, `--out`, the exit code and the loader's stderr are untouched. `--stored` does not use this printer.

## The dispatch's mechanism assumptions, measured

- **H1 holds.** `applyMetaMigrations` builds each todo as `{ ...s, toMajor }` (`packages/spec/src/migrations/chain.ts`), so every todo carries `conversionIds`. On `main` the registry declares exactly two links, and both point into the same hop: `flow-decision-edge-branching-first-match` (18) → `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit` (18), and `time-default-zone-refused` (18) → `time-default-utc-suffix-dropped` (18). No authored link crosses a hop yet. The join runs over the flat `applied` / `todos` arrays, so a cross-hop link pairs by construction. A pin proves it by adding a link from a protocol-18 entry to the protocol-17 conversion `action-execute-to-target` on a real chain result. Across steps, the 108 step conversion ids are unique (0 duplicates).
- **H2 holds, as a copy.** Group 3 keeps every entry, byte-identical, with its header count unchanged. The review line sits in group 2 beside the edits it judges. I did not change it to a move. A move would take the entry out of group 3, and its count would then stop matching the chain's `todos`.
- **H3: one review line per run, not one per edit.** A conversion's edits are contiguous by construction, because the chain replays one conversion at a time and its `apply` emits every edit before the next conversion starts. So a run is "this conversion's edits in this hop". HotCRM had 13 edits by `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit`. One review line per edit would repeat a paragraph-long `replacement` 13 times, which is the noise this card is about. No information is lost: every edit line still names its `conversionId`, and the review line counts the edits above it ("the 2 edits above", or "the edit above" for a run of one). If a conversion's edits were ever split into two runs, each run would get its own review line, so a review line never sits far from its edits.
- **H4: `--stored` does not use `printMigrationReport`.** `runStored` prints `formatStoredMigrationReport` from `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, so this PR does not touch it.

## Evidence: real stacks through `bin/run.js`

Two small authored stacks (`export default { … }` configs) were run with `os migrate meta --from 17`, once on `origin/main` at `315888d660` and once at this PR's head, `c6622657f2`:

- a decision stack: two flows, each with an edge-branched decision with two conditioned out-edges and no `mode`, plus a dashboard `refreshInterval`;
- a time stack: two `time` field defaults, `09:00Z` and `17:30:00+00:00`, plus a dashboard `refreshInterval`.

| | decision stack | time stack |
|:---|:---|:---|
| stdout lines, before → after | 813 → 814 | 813 → 814 |
| stdout diff (timing and `--out` path normalised) | one added line, the review line under the 2 `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit` edits | one added line, the review line under the 2 `time-default-utc-suffix-dropped` edits |
| group 3 entries / header count | 253 = 253 | 253 = 253 |
| `--json` apart from `duration` | identical | identical |
| `--out` snapshot | byte-identical | byte-identical |
| stderr | 0 bytes both runs | 0 bytes both runs |
| exit code (human / `--json`) | 0 / 0 both runs | 0 / 0 both runs |

Before this change, the decision edits printed on lines 13 and 14, and the entry that judges them printed at line 351.

## Tests

The pins extend `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.report-order.test.ts` rather than a new file. That file already holds the printer's helpers (`run`, `appliedLines`, `noticeLines`, `refusalLines`) and the SET pins the pairing must not break, so the pairing pins reuse them, and every pin on this printer stays in one file. The new `PAIR` block adds:

1. the judge prints once, directly under the run of edits it judges, counting them, inside group 2;
2. a run of one says "the edit above";
3. an edit no entry judges prints exactly as before, with no review line under it, and group 2's edit lines equal the chain's, in order;
4. a stack whose applied conversions have no link prints no review line at all;
5. group 3 keeps every entry, the judge included, with the chain's count and bytes;
6. every non-blank line is a header, a refusal, an edit, a notice, or a review line that the declared links call for. The expected review lines are computed without the printer's run logic;
7. every link the registry declares is paired, replayed over the linked conversion's own `fixture.before`, so a link the spec lane adds later is covered when it lands. Anti-vacuity: the two links named in the dispatch are asserted present;
8. a link to a conversion that an earlier step replays pairs across hops.

Measured at `c6622657f2`:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2 src/commands/migrate/meta.report-order.test.ts`: 16 passed (8 existing, 8 new).
- The unit-tier neighbours (`doctor-deprecation-hint-commands`, `meta.stored-flags`, `migrate-meta-strict-factories`, and this file): 4 files, 41 passed.
- `test/migrate-meta-default-range.test.ts`, `test/migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts` and `test/migrate-meta.e2e.test.ts` are integration tier, so they are declared to CI. Their only group 2 assertions are `toContain` checks, which an added line cannot break.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0. The test file is in the `tsc --noEmit` program (`--listFiles`, 1 hit).

**Ablation.** The fix was committed first (`19563f6c4e`). `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `const judges = judgesByConversion(result.todos);` with an empty map (anchor x1 → x0, blob `868eef7e8983` → `542c67cdfca2`). The subject is imported relatively from source, so no build was involved. Result: **5 red** (pins 1, 2, 6, 7 and 8) and **11 green**. The 11 are the 8 order, count and set pins and the 3 control pins: unjudged edit, no-link stack, and group 3 intact. The restore was proven by blob `868eef7e8983` equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, with no paths, at `c6622657f2` (merge base `9b0de7de73`), derived 62 commands. Each was run and its exit code recorded before any pipe. All 62 exited 0. `--ran`: `62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. On the first round, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3, no dist). They were re-run after `pnpm turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs`, and both are green. At reconciliation time, `origin/main` was already 3 commits ahead, and one family file (`scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs`) had changed there. That family reads `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`, which this diff does not touch.

**Lint, as a proven narrowing.** `pnpm lint` is a repo-wide scan owned by CI. Run at `c6622657f2`:

- **Population.** ESLint's own config was asked through its API (`isPathIgnored` and `calculateConfigForFile` against `eslint.config.mjs`, inline config off). `meta.ts` is LINTED with 6 rules and `meta.report-order.test.ts` is LINTED with 5. The changeset is in no config's population.
- **Count.** `--format json` over those 2 files: 2 results, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **Invariance.** `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting: none of its 7 `parserOptions` blocks sets `project`. Its only disk reads at load are two baseline JSON files this diff does not touch. So no untouched file's verdict can move.

## Acceptance notes

- `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md:139-147` describes `Applied N mechanical change(s)` as "one line per rewritten site". With this PR, a judged run also carries a review line. The surface is Tier H governed, and a one-line mention can ride with the group reorder that the previous ACCEPT on this card already left for that surface's next queue entry.
- The `printMigrationReport` docblock cites "242 notices for protocol 18" as the measurement behind direction 1. Today's chain prints 253. It is a dated measurement, not a claim this PR depends on, so it is left as written.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` item `cli.migrate-meta-codemod` locates planted spellings in the `Applied` block by their edit line. The added review lines do not change that.
